methodology.metric: assembled function-body bytes, including prologue/epilogue; external helper bodies excluded
methodology.abi: native compiler calling conventions; extern C does not make the two ABIs identical
methodology.integer_division: Rust unchecked intrinsics match the C valid-input domain; no Rust panic guards
methodology.signed_c_arithmetic: unsigned intermediates and casts; two-complement conversion and arithmetic right shift required
methodology.float_widths: C sizeof assertions prevent double/long double silently becoming f32
methodology.instruction_counts: source mnemonics only; inline db machine code reported separately
methodology.scope: static codegen comparison; no cycle estimates or target runtime equivalence checks
methodology.library_cost: SDCC archive dependency bytes for all supported cases; isolated linked reachable ROM sections for Rust string cases; no startup, entry harness or alignment padding

cases.semantic_note: NUL-terminated output; count excludes NUL; temporary is fully initialized before reads; separate div/mod and derived remainder forms expose quotient reuse
cases.domain: valid non-overlapping allocations unless overlap is explicit; lengths <= 128; NUL strings fit their allocations; output buffers have at least 256 bytes; unsigned arithmetic wraps; parse library variants exclude overflow
cases.c_function: uint16_t format_u16_decimal_divmod(uint8_t *dst, uint16_t value) { uint8_t tmp[20], i = 0; do { uint16_t q = value / 10; uint8_t d = (uint8_t)(value % 10); tmp[i++] = (uint8_t)(d < 10 ? '0' + d : 'a' + d - 10); value = q; } while (value); for (uint8_t j = 0; j < i; ++j) dst[j] = tmp[i - 1 - j]; dst[i] = 0; return i; }

notes.observation: Sangoku function body is 1701 bytes larger than SDCC.
Sangoku has 264 more source instructions referencing SP.
notes.investigate: Inspect value lifetimes, stack slot reuse and argument/result marshaling. SP references include arguments and locals, so they are not a pure spill count.

notes.observation: The source uses different amounts of native register-pair arithmetic.
notes.investigate: Compare native 16-bit address arithmetic with split-byte add/carry sequences. Account for differing algorithms and calling conventions before attributing the size gap.

notes.observation: The emitted source has different branch structure.
notes.investigate: Inspect compare/boolean lowering and fallthrough layout; branch counts alone do not determine cycles.

notes.observation: Sangoku emits register self-copies or an immediate reload of a value just copied from that register.
notes.investigate: Add or improve post-allocation copy cleanup; verify register liveness before removing the original copy.

notes.observation: 160 bytes are emitted through db. They count toward function size but are absent from source mnemonic counts.
Part of the implementation is outside the measured function body.
notes.investigate: Compare reachable helper bodies and calling conventions before judging total code size or speed.

notes.observation: The wrappers use different helper calls or tail transfers.
notes.investigate: A tail transfer can avoid a call/return pair and argument cleanup in the wrapper. An inline loop versus a helper trades shared code size against call overhead; measure runtime before choosing.

notes.observation: Including reachable helpers preserves the function-body ranking.
notes.investigate: This is cold, isolated ROM cost. Shared helpers are charged once per case; an application can amortize them across calls. SDCC cost is at archive-member granularity.

cases.c_function: uint16_t format_u16_decimal_derived(uint8_t *dst, uint16_t value) { uint8_t tmp[20], i = 0; do { uint16_t q = value / 10; uint8_t d = (uint8_t)(value - q * 10); tmp[i++] = (uint8_t)(d < 10 ? '0' + d : 'a' + d - 10); value = q; } while (value); for (uint8_t j = 0; j < i; ++j) dst[j] = tmp[i - 1 - j]; dst[i] = 0; return i; }

analysis.summary: Sangoku function body is 1625 bytes larger than SDCC.
analysis.metric: static function-body bytes; reachable dependency size reported separately when available

notes.observation: Sangoku function body is 1625 bytes larger than SDCC.
Sangoku has 241 more source instructions referencing SP.
notes.investigate: Inspect value lifetimes, stack slot reuse and argument/result marshaling. SP references include arguments and locals, so they are not a pure spill count.

notes.observation: The source uses different amounts of native register-pair arithmetic.
notes.investigate: Compare native 16-bit address arithmetic with split-byte add/carry sequences. Account for differing algorithms and calling conventions before attributing the size gap.

notes.observation: The emitted source has different branch structure.
notes.investigate: Inspect compare/boolean lowering and fallthrough layout; branch counts alone do not determine cycles.

notes.observation: Sangoku emits register self-copies or an immediate reload of a value just copied from that register.
notes.investigate: Add or improve post-allocation copy cleanup; verify register liveness before removing the original copy.

notes.observation: 160 bytes are emitted through db. They count toward function size but are absent from source mnemonic counts.
Part of the implementation is outside the measured function body.
notes.investigate: Compare reachable helper bodies and calling conventions before judging total code size or speed.

notes.observation: The wrappers use different helper calls or tail transfers.
notes.investigate: A tail transfer can avoid a call/return pair and argument cleanup in the wrapper. An inline loop versus a helper trades shared code size against call overhead; measure runtime before choosing.

notes.observation: Including reachable helpers preserves the function-body ranking.
notes.investigate: This is cold, isolated ROM cost. Shared helpers are charged once per case; an application can amortize them across calls. SDCC cost is at archive-member granularity.

notes.observation: NUL-terminated output; count excludes NUL; temporary is fully initialized before reads; separate div/mod and derived remainder forms expose quotient reuse

cases.c_function: uint16_t format_u16_hex(uint8_t *dst, uint16_t value) { uint8_t tmp[20], i = 0; do { uint16_t q = value >> 4; uint8_t d = (uint8_t)(value & 15); tmp[i++] = (uint8_t)(d < 10 ? '0' + d : 'a' + d - 10); value = q; } while (value); for (uint8_t j = 0; j < i; ++j) dst[j] = tmp[i - 1 - j]; dst[i] = 0; return i; }

Sangoku has 292 more source instructions referencing SP.
notes.investigate: Inspect value lifetimes, stack slot reuse and argument/result marshaling. SP references include arguments and locals, so they are not a pure spill count.

notes.investigate: Compare native 16-bit address arithmetic with split-byte add/carry sequences. Account for differing algorithms and calling conventions before attributing the size gap.

notes.observation: The emitted source has different branch structure.
notes.investigate: Inspect compare/boolean lowering and fallthrough layout; branch counts alone do not determine cycles.

notes.observation: Sangoku emits register self-copies or an immediate reload of a value just copied from that register.
notes.investigate: Add or improve post-allocation copy cleanup; verify register liveness before removing the original copy.

Part of the implementation is outside the measured function body.
notes.investigate: Compare reachable helper bodies and calling conventions before judging total code size or speed.

notes.observation: The wrappers use different helper calls or tail transfers.
notes.investigate: A tail transfer can avoid a call/return pair and argument cleanup in the wrapper. An inline loop versus a helper trades shared code size against call overhead; measure runtime before choosing.

notes.observation: Including reachable helpers preserves the function-body ranking.
notes.investigate: This is cold, isolated ROM cost. Shared helpers are charged once per case; an application can amortize them across calls. SDCC cost is at archive-member granularity.

'0' + d : 'a' + d - 10); value = q; } while (value); for (uint8_t j = 0; j < i; ++j) dst[j] = tmp[i - 1 - j]; dst[i] = 0; return i; }

; In: DE = context, A = operand length L in bytes (8 or 16).
; Context: a[L], b[L], op, status. Ops: 0 udiv, 1 urem, 2 sdiv, 3 srem,
; 4 umulhi, 5 smulhi, 6 imul. The result replaces a. Status 1 is a zero
; divisor and 2 is signed division overflow. Every register is clobbered.
; Frame: 0..31 scratch, 32 L, 33 op, 34 context, 36 sign a, 37 sign b,
; 38 bit counter, 39 temporary.

MACRO NEG_IF
    ld hl, sp + \1
    ld c, [hl]
    call __gbc_wide_ctx
IF \2 == 0

    ld l, e
ENDC
    ld a, c
    and a
    call nz, __gbc_wide_neg

.after_a

.mul_result

    ld a, [hl]
    ld hl, sp + 0

    jr z, .mul_copy
    call __gbc_wide_high
.mul_copy
    call __gbc_wide_copy
    add sp, 40
    ret

; Out: DE = a, HL = b, B = L. Keeps C. Only valid one call deep.
__gbc_wide_ctx:
    ld hl, sp + 36
    ld e, [hl]
    inc hl
    ld d, [hl]
    ld hl, sp + 34
    ld b, [hl]
    ld h, 0
    ld l, b
    add hl, de
    ret

; Out: HL = scratch + L, B = L. Only valid one call deep.
__gbc_wide_high:
    ld hl, sp + 2
    ld c, b
    ld b, 0
    add hl, bc
    ld b, c
    ret

; In: HL = array, B = L. Out: A = 1 when negative, else 0.
__gbc_wide_sign:
    ld c, b
    ld b, 0
    add hl, bc
    dec hl
    ld a, [hl]
    rlca
    and 1
    ret

; In: HL = array, B = L, carry in. Out: carry.
__gbc_wide_shl1:
.loop
    rl [hl]
    inc hl
    dec b
    jr nz, .loop
    ret

; In: HL = dst, DE = src, B = L. dst += src; out: carry.
__gbc_wide_add:
    and a
.loop
    ld a, [de]
    adc [hl]
    ld [hli], a
    inc de
    dec b
    jr nz, .loop
    ret

; In: HL = dst, DE = src, B = L. dst -= src; out: carry is borrow.
__gbc_wide_sub:
    and a
.loop
    ld a, [de]
    ld c, a
    ld a, [hl]
    sbc c
    ld [hli], a
    inc de
    dec b
    jr nz, .loop
    ret

; In: HL = array, B = L. Two's complement negate.
__gbc_wide_neg:
    scf
.loop
    ld a, [hl]
    cpl
    adc 0
    ld [hli], a
    dec b
    jr nz, .loop
    ret

; In: HL = src, DE = dst, B = L.
__gbc_wide_copy:
.loop
    ld a, [hli]
    ld [de], a
    inc de
    dec b
    jr nz, .loop
    ret

; In: B = L, A = carry bit. Shifts the 2L byte product right one bit.
__gbc_wide_shr_product:
    ld c, a
    ld a, b
    add a
    ld b, a
    ld hl, sp + 2
    ld d, 0
    ld e, b
    add hl, de
    dec hl
    ld a, c
    rra
.loop
    rr [hl]
    dec hl
    dec b
    jr nz, .loop
    ret

; In: DE = context, A = operand length L in bytes (8 or 16).
; Context: a[L], b[L], op, status. Ops: 0 udiv, 1 urem, 2 sdiv, 3 srem,
; 4 umulhi, 5 smulhi, 6 imul. The result replaces a. Status 1 is a zero
; divisor and 2 is signed division overflow. Every register is clobbered.
; Frame: 0..31 scratch, 32 L, 33 op, 34 context, 36 sign a, 37 sign b,
; 38 bit counter, 39 temporary.

MACRO NEG_IF

    ld c, [hl]
    call __gbc_wide_ctx
IF \2 == 0

    ld l, e

    ld a, c
    and a
    call nz, __gbc_wide_neg

.mul_result

.mul_copy
    call __gbc_wide_copy
    add sp, 40
    ret

; Out: DE = a, HL = b, B = L. Keeps C. Only valid one call deep.
__gbc_wide_ctx:
    ld hl, sp + 36
    ld e, [hl]
    inc hl
    ld d, [hl]
    ld hl, sp + 34
    ld b, [hl]
    ld h, 0
    ld l, b
    add hl, de
    ret

; Out: HL = scratch + L, B = L. Only valid one call deep.
__gbc_wide_high:
    ld hl, sp + 2
    ld c, b
    ld b, 0
    add hl, bc
    ld b, c
    ret

; In: HL = array, B = L. Out: A = 1 when negative, else 0.
__gbc_wide_sign:
    ld c, b
    ld b, 0
    add hl, bc
    dec hl
    ld a, [hl]
    rlca
    and 1
    ret

; In: HL = array, B = L, carry in. Out: carry.
__gbc_wide_shl1:
.loop
    rl [hl]
    inc hl
    dec b
    jr nz, .loop
    ret

; In: HL = dst, DE = src, B = L. dst += src; out: carry.
__gbc_wide_add:
    and a
.loop
    ld a, [de]
    adc [hl]
    ld [hli], a
    inc de
    dec b
    jr nz, .loop
    ret

; In: HL = dst, DE = src, B = L. dst -= src; out: carry is borrow.
__gbc_wide_sub:
    and a
.loop
    ld a, [de]
    ld c, a
    ld a, [hl]
    sbc c
    ld [hli], a
    inc de
    dec b
    jr nz, .loop
    ret

; In: HL = array, B = L. Two's complement negate.
__gbc_wide_neg:
    scf
.loop
    ld a, [hl]
    cpl
    adc 0
    ld [hli], a
    dec b
    jr nz, .loop
    ret

; In: HL = src, DE = dst, B = L.
__gbc_wide_copy:
.loop
    ld a, [hli]
    ld [de], a
    inc de
    dec b
    jr nz, .loop
    ret

; In: B = L, A = carry bit. Shifts the 2L byte product right one bit.
__gbc_wide_shr_product:
    ld c, a
    ld a, b
    add a
    ld b, a
    ld hl, sp + 2
    ld d, 0
    ld e, b
    add hl, de
    dec hl
    ld a, c
    rra
.loop
    rr [hl]
    dec hl
    dec b
    jr nz, .loop
    ret

    add hl, de

    ld a, [hl]
    and 63
    ld c, a
    ret z
.loop

    dec c
    jr nz, .loop
    ret

notes.observation: Sangoku function body is 1877 bytes larger than SDCC.
Sangoku has 269 more source instructions referencing SP.
notes.investigate: Inspect value lifetimes, stack slot reuse and argument/result marshaling. SP references include arguments and locals, so they are not a pure spill count.

notes.observation: The source uses different amounts of native register-pair arithmetic.
notes.investigate: Compare native 16-bit address arithmetic with split-byte add/carry sequences. Account for differing algorithms and calling conventions before attributing the size gap.

notes.observation: The emitted source has different branch structure.
notes.investigate: Inspect compare/boolean lowering and fallthrough layout; branch counts alone do not determine cycles.

notes.observation: Sangoku emits register self-copies or an immediate reload of a value just copied from that register.
notes.investigate: Add or improve post-allocation copy cleanup; verify register liveness before removing the original copy.

notes.observation: 280 bytes are emitted through db. They count toward function size but are absent from source mnemonic counts.
Part of the implementation is outside the measured function body.
notes.investigate: Compare reachable helper bodies and calling conventions before judging total code size or speed.

notes.observation: The wrappers use different helper calls or tail transfers.
notes.investigate: A tail transfer can avoid a call/return pair and argument cleanup in the wrapper. An inline loop versus a helper trades shared code size against call overhead; measure runtime before choosing.

notes.observation: Including reachable helpers preserves the function-body ranking.
notes.investigate: This is cold, isolated ROM cost. Shared helpers are charged once per case; an application can amortize them across calls. SDCC cost is at archive-member granularity.

analysis.summary: Sangoku function body is 1712 bytes larger than SDCC.
analysis.metric: static function-body bytes; reachable dependency size reported separately when available

notes.observation: Sangoku function body is 1712 bytes larger than SDCC.
Sangoku has 267 more source instructions referencing SP.
notes.investigate: Inspect value lifetimes, stack slot reuse and argument/result marshaling. SP references include arguments and locals, so they are not a pure spill count.

notes.observation: The source uses different amounts of native register-pair arithmetic.
notes.investigate: Compare native 16-bit address arithmetic with split-byte add/carry sequences. Account for differing algorithms and calling conventions before attributing the size gap.

notes.observation: The emitted source has different branch structure.
notes.investigate: Inspect compare/boolean lowering and fallthrough layout; branch counts alone do not determine cycles.

notes.observation: Sangoku emits register self-copies or an immediate reload of a value just copied from that register.
notes.investigate: Add or improve post-allocation copy cleanup; verify register liveness before removing the original copy.

notes.observation: 160 bytes are emitted through db. They count toward function size but are absent from source mnemonic counts.
Part of the implementation is outside the measured function body.
notes.investigate: Compare reachable helper bodies and calling conventions before judging total code size or speed.

notes.observation: The wrappers use different helper calls or tail transfers.
notes.investigate: A tail transfer can avoid a call/return pair and argument cleanup in the wrapper. An inline loop versus a helper trades shared code size against call overhead; measure runtime before choosing.

notes.observation: Including reachable helpers preserves the function-body ranking.
notes.investigate: This is cold, isolated ROM cost. Shared helpers are charged once per case; an application can amortize them across calls. SDCC cost is at archive-member granularity.

notes.observation: NUL-terminated output; count excludes NUL; temporary is fully initialized before reads; separate div/mod and derived remainder forms expose quotient reuse

'0' + d : 'a' + d - 10); value = q; } while (value); for (uint8_t j = 0; j < i; ++j) dst[j] = tmp[i - 1 - j]; dst[i] = 0; return i; }

MACRO NEG_IF

.mul_copy

; Out: DE = a, HL = b, B = L. Keeps C. Only valid one call deep.
__gbc_wide_ctx:
    ld hl, sp + 36
    ld e, [hl]
    inc hl
    ld d, [hl]
    ld hl, sp + 34
    ld b, [hl]
    ld h, 0
    ld l, b
    add hl, de
    ret

; Out: HL = scratch + L, B = L. Only valid one call deep.
__gbc_wide_high:
    ld hl, sp + 2
    ld c, b
    ld b, 0
    add hl, bc
    ld b, c
    ret

; In: HL = array, B = L. Out: A = 1 when negative, else 0.
__gbc_wide_sign:
    ld c, b
    ld b, 0
    add hl, bc
    dec hl
    ld a, [hl]
    rlca
    and 1
    ret

; In: HL = array, B = L, carry in. Out: carry.
__gbc_wide_shl1:
.loop
    rl [hl]
    inc hl
    dec b
    jr nz, .loop
    ret

; In: HL = dst, DE = src, B = L. dst += src; out: carry.
__gbc_wide_add:
    and a
.loop
    ld a, [de]
    adc [hl]
    ld [hli], a
    inc de
    dec b
    jr nz, .loop
    ret

; In: HL = dst, DE = src, B = L. dst -= src; out: carry is borrow.
__gbc_wide_sub:
    and a
.loop
    ld a, [de]
    ld c, a
    ld a, [hl]
    sbc c
    ld [hli], a
    inc de
    dec b
    jr nz, .loop
    ret

; In: HL = array, B = L. Two's complement negate.
__gbc_wide_neg:
    scf
.loop
    ld a, [hl]
    cpl
    adc 0
    ld [hli], a
    dec b
    jr nz, .loop
    ret

; In: HL = src, DE = dst, B = L.
__gbc_wide_copy:
.loop
    ld a, [hli]
    ld [de], a
    inc de
    dec b
    jr nz, .loop
    ret

; In: B = L, A = carry bit. Shifts the 2L byte product right one bit.
__gbc_wide_shr_product:
    ld c, a
    ld a, b
    add a
    ld b, a
    ld hl, sp + 2
    ld d, 0
    ld e, b
    add hl, de
    dec hl
    ld a, c
    rra
.loop
    rr [hl]
    dec hl
    dec b
    jr nz, .loop
    ret

; 38 bit counter, 39 temporary.

MACRO NEG_IF

; Out: DE = a, HL = b, B = L. Keeps C. Only valid one call deep.
__gbc_wide_ctx:
    ld hl, sp + 36
    ld e, [hl]
    inc hl
    ld d, [hl]
    ld hl, sp + 34
    ld b, [hl]
    ld h, 0
    ld l, b
    add hl, de
    ret

; Out: HL = scratch + L, B = L. Only valid one call deep.
__gbc_wide_high:
    ld hl, sp + 2
    ld c, b
    ld b, 0
    add hl, bc
    ld b, c
    ret

; In: HL = array, B = L. Out: A = 1 when negative, else 0.
__gbc_wide_sign:
    ld c, b
    ld b, 0
    add hl, bc
    dec hl
    ld a, [hl]
    rlca
    and 1
    ret

; In: HL = array, B = L, carry in. Out: carry.
__gbc_wide_shl1:
.loop
    rl [hl]
    inc hl
    dec b
    jr nz, .loop
    ret

; In: HL = dst, DE = src, B = L. dst += src; out: carry.
__gbc_wide_add:
    and a
.loop
    ld a, [de]
    adc [hl]
    ld [hli], a
    inc de
    dec b
    jr nz, .loop
    ret

; In: HL = dst, DE = src, B = L. dst -= src; out: carry is borrow.
__gbc_wide_sub:
    and a
.loop
    ld a, [de]
    ld c, a
    ld a, [hl]
    sbc c
    ld [hli], a
    inc de
    dec b
    jr nz, .loop
    ret

; In: HL = array, B = L. Two's complement negate.
__gbc_wide_neg:
    scf
.loop
    ld a, [hl]
    cpl
    adc 0
    ld [hli], a
    dec b
    jr nz, .loop
    ret

; In: HL = src, DE = dst, B = L.
__gbc_wide_copy:
.loop
    ld a, [hli]
    ld [de], a
    inc de
    dec b
    jr nz, .loop
    ret

; In: B = L, A = carry bit. Shifts the 2L byte product right one bit.
__gbc_wide_shr_product:
    ld c, a
    ld a, b
    add a
    ld b, a
    ld hl, sp + 2
    ld d, 0
    ld e, b
    add hl, de
    dec hl
    ld a, c
    rra
.loop
    rr [hl]
    dec hl
    dec b
    jr nz, .loop
    ret

notes.observation: Sangoku function body is 1875 bytes larger than SDCC.
Sangoku has 268 more source instructions referencing SP.
notes.investigate: Inspect value lifetimes, stack slot reuse and argument/result marshaling. SP references include arguments and locals, so they are not a pure spill count.

notes.observation: The source uses different amounts of native register-pair arithmetic.
notes.investigate: Compare native 16-bit address arithmetic with split-byte add/carry sequences. Account for differing algorithms and calling conventions before attributing the size gap.

notes.observation: The emitted source has different branch structure.
notes.investigate: Inspect compare/boolean lowering and fallthrough layout; branch counts alone do not determine cycles.

notes.observation: Sangoku emits register self-copies or an immediate reload of a value just copied from that register.
notes.investigate: Add or improve post-allocation copy cleanup; verify register liveness before removing the original copy.

notes.observation: 280 bytes are emitted through db. They count toward function size but are absent from source mnemonic counts.
Part of the implementation is outside the measured function body.
notes.investigate: Compare reachable helper bodies and calling conventions before judging total code size or speed.

notes.observation: The wrappers use different helper calls or tail transfers.
notes.investigate: A tail transfer can avoid a call/return pair and argument cleanup in the wrapper. An inline loop versus a helper trades shared code size against call overhead; measure runtime before choosing.

notes.observation: Including reachable helpers preserves the function-body ranking.
notes.investigate: This is cold, isolated ROM cost. Shared helpers are charged once per case; an application can amortize them across calls. SDCC cost is at archive-member granularity.

analysis.summary: Sangoku function body is 285 bytes larger than SDCC.
analysis.metric: static function-body bytes; reachable dependency size reported separately when available

notes.observation: Sangoku function body is 285 bytes larger than SDCC.
Sangoku has 46 more source instructions referencing SP.
notes.investigate: Inspect value lifetimes, stack slot reuse and argument/result marshaling. SP references include arguments and locals, so they are not a pure spill count.

notes.observation: The source uses different amounts of native register-pair arithmetic.
notes.investigate: Compare native 16-bit address arithmetic with split-byte add/carry sequences. Account for differing algorithms and calling conventions before attributing the size gap.

notes.observation: The emitted source has different branch structure.
notes.investigate: Inspect compare/boolean lowering and fallthrough layout; branch counts alone do not determine cycles.

notes.observation: Sangoku emits register self-copies or an immediate reload of a value just copied from that register.
notes.investigate: Add or improve post-allocation copy cleanup; verify register liveness before removing the original copy.

notes.observation: 20 bytes are emitted through db. They count toward function size but are absent from source mnemonic counts.
Part of the implementation is outside the measured function body.
notes.investigate: Compare reachable helper bodies and calling conventions before judging total code size or speed.

notes.observation: The wrappers use different helper calls or tail transfers.
notes.investigate: A tail transfer can avoid a call/return pair and argument cleanup in the wrapper. An inline loop versus a helper trades shared code size against call overhead; measure runtime before choosing.

notes.observation: Including reachable helpers preserves the function-body ranking.
notes.investigate: This is cold, isolated ROM cost. Shared helpers are charged once per case; an application can amortize them across calls. SDCC cost is at archive-member granularity.

notes.observation: Sangoku function body is 457 bytes larger than SDCC.
Sangoku has 86 more source instructions referencing SP.
notes.investigate: Inspect value lifetimes, stack slot reuse and argument/result marshaling. SP references include arguments and locals, so they are not a pure spill count.

notes.observation: The source uses different amounts of native register-pair arithmetic.
notes.investigate: Compare native 16-bit address arithmetic with split-byte add/carry sequences. Account for differing algorithms and calling conventions before attributing the size gap.

notes.observation: The emitted source has different branch structure.
notes.investigate: Inspect compare/boolean lowering and fallthrough layout; branch counts alone do not determine cycles.

notes.observation: 24 bytes are emitted through db. They count toward function size but are absent from source mnemonic counts.
Part of the implementation is outside the measured function body.
notes.investigate: Compare reachable helper bodies and calling conventions before judging total code size or speed.

notes.observation: The wrappers use different helper calls or tail transfers.
notes.investigate: A tail transfer can avoid a call/return pair and argument cleanup in the wrapper. An inline loop versus a helper trades shared code size against call overhead; measure runtime before choosing.

notes.observation: Including reachable helpers preserves the function-body ranking.
notes.investigate: This is cold, isolated ROM cost. Shared helpers are charged once per case; an application can amortize them across calls. SDCC cost is at archive-member granularity.

__gbc_mul16::
    ld d, c
    ld e, b
    ld c, a
    ld hl, sp + 2
    ld a, [hl]
    ld hl, 0
    or a
    jp z, .narrow
    REPT 16
        MUL16_STEP
    ENDR
    jr .done
.narrow
    ld a, c
    REPT 8
        MUL16_NARROW_STEP
    ENDR
.done
    ld a, l
    ld b, h
    ret

notes.observation: Including reachable helpers preserves the function-body ranking.
notes.investigate: This is cold, isolated ROM cost. Shared helpers are charged once per case; an application can amortize them across calls. SDCC cost is at archive-member granularity.
